- tests/test_audit_plans_command.py: lines 15-16 and 31-33 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Unconditionally reassigning COMMAND = TEMPLATE_COMMAND whenever TEMPLATE_COMMAND.is_file() is true sets COMMAND to the template path. In test_template_parity(), the condition if COMMAND != TEMPLATE_COMMAND: then always evaluates to False, bypassing the parity assertion entirely. Subsequent contract tests in this module inspect the template command rather than the repository root command at .claude/commands/audit-plans.md.
  WHY: Discrepancies between .claude/commands/audit-plans.md and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md pass CI undetected, allowing stale or divergent root commands to escape validation.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 30-31 and 1012-1014 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Line 30 was modified from checking if not GUARD_PATH.is_file(): to checking if TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH.is_file():. Because TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH exists on disk, GUARD_PATH is unconditionally reassigned to TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH even when .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py is present. Consequently, in test_template_copies_are_identical(), the condition if GUARD_PATH != TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH: always evaluates to False, permanently disabling the parity check. Furthermore, the test suite exercises only the template hook instead of the root hook.
  WHY: Drift or regressions in the root .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py hook cannot be caught by CI, defeating the parity verification contract.
- tests/test_claude_anthropic_relay.py: lines 180-183 (and scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py lines 102-127) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: In test_broker_rejects_client_authorization, connection.request() sends headers and body across the Unix domain socket. In scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py, do_POST inspects the headers and immediately calls _reject(400) upon finding an Authorization header on the broker socket. _reject sends a 400 response and closes the connection without reading the incoming request body. When the server closes the socket while the client is still writing the request body, the write triggers a socket broken pipe error.
  WHY: In CI job tests-hooks-and-orchestrator (run 37210976001), test_broker_rejects_client_authorization fails with BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe instead of reading HTTP 400, causing tests-hooks-and-orchestrator and the aggregate lint check to fail.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- tests/test_audit_plans_command.py: lines 15-16 (added fallback) and lines 31-35 (test_template_parity) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new fallback `if TEMPLATE_COMMAND.is_file(): COMMAND = TEMPLATE_COMMAND` reassigns COMMAND to the same path as TEMPLATE_COMMAND whenever the template exists. Because COMMAND and TEMPLATE_COMMAND then point at the same file, the `if COMMAND != TEMPLATE_COMMAND:` guard inside `test_template_parity` is always False, and the parity comparison is skipped. In a checkout that retains both the root `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md` and the workflow-templates twin (e.g. a consumer repo, a stale worktree, or a CI runner on an older ref), the test never reads the root copy and never catches root-template drift.
  WHY: When the template exists, the test only asserts the template's own file exists; it never compares the root and template contents, so any future divergence between the root command and its twin goes undetected by the parity check.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py: line 30 (changed condition) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fallback condition was flipped from `if not GUARD_PATH.is_file():` (use template only when root is absent) to `if TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH.is_file():` (use template whenever the template exists, even if the root guard also exists). This makes `GUARD_PATH == TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH` true in any checkout that has the template, so the `if GUARD_PATH != TEMPLATE_GUARD_PATH:` guard in `test_template_copies_are_identical` is always False and the guard parity comparison is skipped. The settings assertion immediately below stays unconditional, so the inconsistency between the two fallbacks inside the same test function is also visible.
  WHY: When both `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` and the template twin are present (consumer repos, stale checkouts), the test never reads the root copy, so root-template drift in the guard hook is not caught. The settings fallback (`if not SETTINGS_PATH.is_file():`) was not updated to match, so the two fallbacks inside the same file now disagree about which copy is authoritative.
- tests/test_audit_plans_command.py: lines 15-16 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When `TEMPLATE_COMMAND` does not exist (`is_file()` returns False), `COMMAND` is left pointing at the root path `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md`, which the source repo has retired. If the root path is also absent, the fixture at lines 18-25 (`@pytest.fixture(scope="module") def text(): return COMMAND.read_text(...)`) raises `FileNotFoundError` at collection time, surfacing as an opaque collection failure rather than a descriptive assertion that names the missing path.
  WHY: A checkout where both root and template command files are absent fails pytest collection with `FileNotFoundError` instead of an assertion that explicitly says both command files are missing.
- Requirement: PR description states "Heal and related suites: 412 passed. Every other test touching the changed workflows ran on this branch and on a clean main side by side, with identical results." and "Heal suites: 169 passed." implying the PR should leave the CI green. The current `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` CI failure on this PR head (run 37210976001) is `test_broker_rejects_client_authorization` raising `BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe` in tests/test_claude_anthropic_relay.py, and the log shows the `lint` aggregate failing because of that job. The LAST RUN DIFF makes no change to tests/test_claude_anthropic_relay.py, scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py, or tests/test_gh_api_write_guard.py, so the pre-existing failure mode that PR comment 10 says "stays red until both of these are fixed on main" is not addressed by the LAST RUN DIFF.
